text:
ConocoPhillips dropped 6.1% today after oil prices fell sharply on news that Saudi Arabia will resume pipeline operations within days and is offering additional crude supplies through ship-to-ship transfers. The broader energy sector sold off as these developments eased concerns about supply disruptions from recent attacks on Saudi infrastructure, removing a key prop that had supported prices—US crude fell to $107 per barrel from around $141 just yesterday.

The stock's sharp reversal also reflects a widening gap between US and global oil prices (US at $107 vs. world crude at $131), which can squeeze refining and integrated oil company profits. Major producers like ConocoPhillips benefit when supply fears keep prices elevated; when those fears ease and supplies look adequate, the premium evaporates.
